title: GMAT Focus Data Insights Practice Test 9
instructions: Original exam-style practice test with answers and explanations.

questions.prompt:
Annual visitors and staff at five heritage sites:

Alnwick: 7,300 visitors, 21 staff
Bewdley: 12,800 visitors, 44 staff
Corbridge: 4,600 visitors, 11 staff
Dulverton: 10,100 visitors, 34 staff
Eynsham: 8,700 visitors, 25 staff

Which site receives the most visitors per member of staff?
options: A. Alnwick
B. Bewdley
C. Dulverton
D. Corbridge
E. Eynsham
questions.explanation: Visitors divided by staff: Alnwick 348, Bewdley 291, Corbridge 418, Dulverton 297, Eynsham 348. Corbridge is highest. The busiest site also employs the most people, so it is not the most stretched per head.

questions.prompt:
Annual apprenticeship starts at a manufacturer:

2021: 268
2022: 331
2023: 322
2024: 402
2025: 445

In which year was the percentage rise over the previous year greatest?
options: E. Starts fell in every year
questions.explanation: Year on year: 2022 +23.5%, 2023 -2.7%, 2024 +24.8%, 2025 +10.7%. 2024 is largest at 24.8%. 2024 adds more starts in absolute terms but from a larger base.

questions.prompt:
A consultancy's costs by category:

Salaries: 51%
Premises: 18%
Equipment: 13%
Travel: 9%
Training: 6%
Other: 3%

What is the smallest number of categories that together account for at least 75% of costs?
options: A. Two
B. Three
C. Four
D. Five
E. Six
questions.explanation: Largest first: 51 + 18 = 69%, short of 75. Adding Equipment reaches 82%. So 3 categories are needed.

questions.prompt:
Seven readings, in order: 18, 19, 19, 21, 24, 27, 62

Which statement about these readings is accurate?
options: A. The mean and the median are equal
B. The mode is greater than the median
C. The mean is smaller than the median
D. The mean is more than twice the median
E. The range is greater than the mean and the mean is greater than the median
questions.explanation: Mean 27.14, median 21, mode 19, range 44. So range > mean > median, the ordering a single large reading produces — though the mean is not twice the median.

questions.prompt:
Two water tariffs, each a standing charge plus a rate per cubic metre:

Tariff One: GBP 95.00 a year plus GBP 0.32 per cubic metre
Tariff Two: GBP 240.00 a year plus GBP 0.11 per cubic metre

Select the usage at which the two cost the same AND the cheaper tariff at 900 cubic metres a year.
options: A. 690 cubic metres; Tariff One is cheaper at 900
B. 500 cubic metres; Tariff Two is cheaper at 900
C. 690 cubic metres; Tariff Two is cheaper at 900
D. 690 cubic metres; the two cost the same at 900
E. The two never cost the same
questions.explanation: Equal when 95 + 0.32u = 240 + 0.11u, so u = 145/0.21 = 690 cubic metres. At 900: One costs GBP 383.00, Two costs GBP 339.00, so Tariff Two is cheaper above the crossover.

questions.prompt:
Two sites last quarter:

Site P: 640 orders, average order value GBP 18.50
Site Q: 210 orders, average order value GBP 41.00

Select the site with the higher total sales AND the site with the higher average order value.
options: A. Site P on total sales; Site Q on average order value
B. Site P on both measures
C. Site Q on total sales; Site P on average order value
D. Site Q on both measures
E. The two sites are equal on both measures
questions.explanation: Totals: Site P GBP 11,840.00, Site Q GBP 8,610.00. Average order value is given: Site P GBP 18.50, Site Q GBP 41.00. Volume and value point to different sites, so neither figure alone ranks them.

questions.prompt:
A vehicle can be bought for GBP 22,000.00, kept 8 years, sold for GBP 4,000.00, with running costs of GBP 1,350.00 a year; or leased for GBP 4,200.00 a year with running costs included.

Select the cheaper option per year AND the annual difference.
options: A. Leasing; GBP 600.00
B. Buying; GBP 500.00
C. Leasing; GBP 900.00
D. Buying; GBP 1,200.00
E. Buying; GBP 600.00
questions.explanation: Owning costs GBP 18,000.00 of depreciation over 8 years, GBP 2,250.00 a year, plus GBP 1,350.00 running: GBP 3,600.00. Leasing is GBP 4,200.00. Buying is cheaper by GBP 600.00 a year.

questions.prompt:
A conference organiser has fixed costs of GBP 56,000.00. Each ticket sells for GBP 220.00 and costs GBP 132.00 to service.

Select the number of tickets needed to break even AND the number needed for a profit of GBP 30,000.00.
options: A. 637 to break even; 1,274 for the target
B. 637 to break even; 978 for the target
C. 500 to break even; 978 for the target
D. 637 to break even; 1,200 for the target
E. 700 to break even; 1,400 for the target
questions.explanation: Contribution is GBP 88.00 a ticket. Break-even is GBP 56,000.00 / GBP 88.00 = 637 tickets. Covering GBP 86,000.00 needs 978.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): population — Region A 118,000, Region B 64,000, Region C 92,000

SOURCE 2 (table): reported cases — Region A 742, Region B 508, Region C 469

SOURCE 3 (memo): "Resources should go where the rate per head of population is highest."

Which region should receive resources on that criterion?
options: A. Region A
B. Region B
C. Region C
D. The three regions are equal
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Cases per 10,000 people: Region A 62.9, Region B 79.4, Region C 51.0. Region B is highest. Region A reports the most cases in total and has the largest population.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (memo): "Average handling time fell from 9.2 to 6.4 minutes after the new script was introduced."

SOURCE 2 (note): "Calls transferred to a specialist team are timed separately from the point of transfer."

SOURCE 3 (table): transfers rose from 4% to 23% of calls.

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Customers are served 30% faster
B. The script has no effect on handling time
C. Handling time rose once transfers are counted
D. Much of the fall reflects time moved to a separately timed team rather than removed
E. Transfers are unrelated to handling time
questions.explanation: Transfers rose almost sixfold while their duration stopped counting toward the measure, so part of the fall is reclassification. Option C overstates in the other direction: the sources do not give the transferred time, only that it is excluded.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (table): pallets handled — Depot 1 18,600, Depot 2 5,400, Depot 3 11,200

SOURCE 2 (table): damage rate — Depot 1 1.7%, Depot 2 6.3%, Depot 3 3.1%

SOURCE 3 (email): "Each damaged pallet costs the same to write off, so start where the most are damaged."

Which depot should be tackled first?
options: A. Depot 3
B. Depot 1
C. Depot 2
D. All three damage the same number
E. Cannot be determined from the sources
questions.explanation: Damaged pallets are volume multiplied by rate: Depot 1 316, Depot 2 340, Depot 3 347. Depot 3 is highest. Depot 2 has much the worst rate but handles the fewest pallets.

questions.prompt:
SOURCE 1 (report): "Turnover per employee rose from GBP 84,000.00 to GBP 96,000.00."

SOURCE 2 (table): employees fell from 250 to 190 over the same period.

SOURCE 3 (email): "The board wants to know what happened to total turnover."

Which statement is best supported?
options: A. Total turnover rose by about 14%
B. Total turnover was unchanged
C. Total turnover fell by about 13%
D. Total turnover cannot be calculated from these sources
E. Employees became less productive
questions.explanation: Total turnover is employees multiplied by turnover per employee: before, 250 × GBP 84,000.00 = GBP 21,000,000.00; after, 190 × GBP 96,000.00 = GBP 18,240,000.00 — a fall of about 13%. Source 1 alone supports option A, which is why the headcount table decides it.

questions.prompt:
Three adult tickets and two child tickets cost GBP 97.00. What does one adult ticket cost?

(1) A child ticket costs GBP 11.00.
(2) An adult ticket costs more than twice a child ticket.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1): 3a + 22 = 97, so a = GBP 25.00 - sufficient. (2) only bounds the price from below, allowing many values. Note that (1) and (2) agree, since 25 is more than twice 11.

questions.prompt:
A cyclist covered 96 km. How long did the ride take?

(1) The average speed was 24 km/h.
(2) The ride began at 09:00 and ended at 13:00.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: From (1): 96 / 24 = 4 hours - sufficient. From (2): 09:00 to 13:00 is also 4 hours - sufficient. The two agree, so either alone answers the question.

questions.prompt:
How many of a club's 90 members renewed?

(1) More than half renewed.
(2) The number who did not renew was one fifth of the number who did.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: (1) only bounds the answer above 45. (2) gives r + r/5 = 90, so r = 75 - sufficient alone, and consistent with (1).

questions.prompt:
Is the product of two integers even?

(1) Their sum is odd.
(2) Their difference is odd.
options: A. Statement (1) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (2) alone is not sufficient.
B. Statement (2) ALONE is sufficient, but statement (1) alone is not sufficient.
C. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER alone is sufficient.
D. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.
E. Statements (1) and (2) TOGETHER are not sufficient.
questions.explanation: An odd sum means one integer is even and one odd, so the product is even - sufficient. An odd difference means the same thing, so (2) is sufficient too. Each alone settles it.

questions.prompt:
Which branch earns the most in fees per adviser?

Branch | Advisers | Complaints per 100 cases | Annual fees | Satisfaction
Alverton | 74 | 3.8 | GBP 214,000.00 | 59
Beckhampton | 129 | 2.4 | GBP 361,000.00 | 81
Cheriton | 52 | 5.6 | GBP 158,000.00 | 64
Dinsdale | 106 | 3.1 | GBP 298,000.00 | 73
Elmsfield | 158 | 1.8 | GBP 442,000.00 | 55
Fenstanton | 88 | 4.6 | GBP 251,000.00 | 70
options: A. Alverton
B. Beckhampton
C. Cheriton
D. Dinsdale
E. Elmsfield
questions.explanation: Fees divided by advisers: Alverton GBP 2,891.89, Beckhampton GBP 2,798.45, Cheriton GBP 3,038.46, Dinsdale GBP 2,811.32, Elmsfield GBP 2,797.47, Fenstanton GBP 2,852.27. Cheriton is highest. The branch with the largest fee income also has the most advisers.

questions.prompt:
How many branches have a complaint rate above the mean for the six?

Branch | Advisers | Complaints per 100 cases | Annual fees | Satisfaction
Alverton | 74 | 3.8 | GBP 214,000.00 | 59
Beckhampton | 129 | 2.4 | GBP 361,000.00 | 81
Cheriton | 52 | 5.6 | GBP 158,000.00 | 64
Dinsdale | 106 | 3.1 | GBP 298,000.00 | 73
Elmsfield | 158 | 1.8 | GBP 442,000.00 | 55
Fenstanton | 88 | 4.6 | GBP 251,000.00 | 70
options: A. One
B. Two
C. Four
D. Three
E. Five
questions.explanation: Mean complaint rate is (3.8 + 2.4 + 5.6 + 3.1 + 1.8 + 4.6) / 6 = 3.55. Above it: Alverton 3.8, Cheriton 5.6, Fenstanton 4.6 — 3 branches.

questions.prompt:
Taking the rate as complaints per 100 cases and each adviser as handling 100 cases a year, which branch receives the most complaints?

Branch | Advisers | Complaints per 100 cases | Annual fees | Satisfaction
Alverton | 74 | 3.8 | GBP 214,000.00 | 59
Beckhampton | 129 | 2.4 | GBP 361,000.00 | 81
Cheriton | 52 | 5.6 | GBP 158,000.00 | 64
Dinsdale | 106 | 3.1 | GBP 298,000.00 | 73
Elmsfield | 158 | 1.8 | GBP 442,000.00 | 55
Fenstanton | 88 | 4.6 | GBP 251,000.00 | 70
options: A. Alverton
B. Beckhampton
C. Dinsdale
D. Elmsfield
E. Fenstanton
questions.explanation: Complaints are advisers multiplied by the rate per hundred cases: Alverton 281, Beckhampton 310, Cheriton 291, Dinsdale 329, Elmsfield 284, Fenstanton 405. Fenstanton is highest. The worst rate belongs to Cheriton, which has the fewest advisers.

questions.prompt:
Rank the branches by fee income and separately by satisfaction, highest first in each. Which branch's two ranks differ most?

Branch | Advisers | Complaints per 100 cases | Annual fees | Satisfaction
Alverton | 74 | 3.8 | GBP 214,000.00 | 59
Beckhampton | 129 | 2.4 | GBP 361,000.00 | 81
Cheriton | 52 | 5.6 | GBP 158,000.00 | 64
Dinsdale | 106 | 3.1 | GBP 298,000.00 | 73
Elmsfield | 158 | 1.8 | GBP 442,000.00 | 55
Fenstanton | 88 | 4.6 | GBP 251,000.00 | 70
options: A. Elmsfield
B. Alverton
C. Beckhampton
D. Cheriton
E. Fenstanton
questions.explanation: By fees: Elmsfield, Beckhampton, Dinsdale, Fenstanton, Alverton, Cheriton. By satisfaction: Beckhampton, Dinsdale, Fenstanton, Cheriton, Alverton, Elmsfield. Rank gaps: Alverton 0, Beckhampton 1, Cheriton 2, Dinsdale 1, Elmsfield 5, Fenstanton 1. Elmsfield differs by 5.
